en: Team: today's bake list is ready
Hello, the bake list for {date} is ready: {orders_due} orders, {units_due} units and {trays_needed} tray loads.
Hello {baker}, you start the {product} bake on {date}: {batches} batch(es), {oven_minutes} oven minutes.
Team: the decorating plan for the day
Hello {decorator}, your decorating plan: order {order_id}, {product}, {decoration}, {hours} hours, due on {due_date}.
Team: tomorrow is full, come early
Hello, {date} is full: {orders_due} orders and {trays_needed} tray loads. Please come early.
Hello {person}, can you take the shift on {date} from {start_time}, {shift_hours} hours?
Team: an order needs your approval
Hello, order {order_id} for {product} due on {due_date} needs your approval before baking.
Hello, the oven is booked on {date} in the {block} block for {program}: {tray_loads} tray loads.
Team: a rush order was added
Hello, a rush order {order_id} was added for {due_date}: {qty} x {product}. Please check the plan.
Team: check the fridge space tonight
Hello, on {date} the fridge holds {slots_used} slots of {capacity}. Please check the space tonight.
Team: thanks for covering the busy day
Hello {person}, thank you for covering the busy day on {date}: {hours} hours and {tasks} tasks.
Hello, the standing order bake for {account}: {units_delivery} x {product} on {weekdays}.
Team: a time off request needs an answer
Hello, {person} asks for time off from {from_date} to {to_date} ({kind}). Please answer.
Decorator: your workload is too high
Hello {person}, your workload on {date} is {hours} hours against {capacity_hours} hours of capacity. We will move some work.
Hello {decorator}, the decorating queue: order {order_id}, {decoration}, due on {due_date}, {hours} hours.
Hello {decorator}, the design brief of order {order_id} changed. Please read it again before you start. Due on {due_date}.
Hello {decorator}, can order {order_id} ({product}) move to an earlier day? It needs {hours} hours and is due on {due_date}.
Baker: the batch list for the day
Hello {baker}, your batch on {date}: {product}, {batches} batch(es), {tray_loads} tray loads.
Hello {baker}, the recipe of {product} was updated. Please check the quantities before the bake on {date}.
Baker: a tray load is spare in the oven
Hello, {free_trays} tray loads are free in the {block} block on {date}. Please use them for the next bake.
Baker: the bread bake starts earlier
Hello, the {program} on {date} starts earlier in the {block} block. Please be ready.
Owner: the oven is over capacity
Hello, the oven on {date} needs {trays_needed} tray loads of {tray_capacity}. Please decide what to move.
Hello, the fridge on {date} holds {slots_used} slots of {capacity}. Please check the plan.
Owner: a team member is overloaded
Hello, {person} has {hours} hours on {date} against {capacity_hours} hours of capacity.
Owner: the holiday peak needs helpers
Hello, {period} starts on {from_date}: {expected_orders} orders and {extra_hours} extra staff hours. Please book the helpers.
Owner: the equipment service is due
Hello, the service of {equipment} is due on {next_service}, in {days_to_service} days.
Client: your order is in production
Hello {client}, your order {order_id} for {product} is in production. It is due on {due_date}.
Client: your order will be a bit later
Hello {client}, your order {order_id} will be ready a little later than planned on {due_date}. We are sorry and we will tell you the new time soon.
Hello, {equipment} needs a service. It was last serviced on {last_service}. Can you visit before {next_service}?
Daily production plan of {set:company} for {col:plan.date} ({col:plan.weekday}), dated {today}.

Orders due: {col:plan.orders_due}, units due: {col:plan.units_due}. Hours planned: {col:plan.hours_planned} (bake {col:plan.bake_hours}, decorate {col:plan.decorate_hours}, pack {col:plan.pack_hours}), of which wholesale {col:plan.wholesale_hours}.

Oven: {col:plan.trays_needed} tray loads of {col:plan.tray_capacity}, load {col:plan.oven_load}, {col:plan.oven_flag}. Fridge: {col:plan.fridge_needed} slots of {col:plan.fridge_capacity}, load {col:plan.fridge_load}, {col:plan.fridge_flag}.
Team hours available: {col:plan.staff_hours}, staff load {col:plan.staff_load}. Pin the plan where the team starts the day and tell the head baker before any change.
Weekly production plan line for a day
Weekly production plan of {set:company}, dated {today}. Week: {col:plan.week_label}. Day: {col:plan.date} ({col:plan.weekday}).
On this day {col:plan.orders_due} orders and {col:plan.units_due} units are due. Hours planned {col:plan.hours_planned} against {col:plan.staff_hours} team hours (staff load {col:plan.staff_load}).
Tray loads needed {col:plan.trays_needed} of {col:plan.tray_capacity} ({col:plan.oven_flag}). Fridge slots {col:plan.fridge_needed} of {col:plan.fridge_capacity} ({col:plan.fridge_flag}).
Print one line for each day of the week and check the days marked nearly full or over capacity first.
Decorator work sheet for a day
Decorator work sheet of {set:company} for {col:load.date}, dated {today}.
Person: {col:load.person} ({col:load.role}). Tasks: {col:load.tasks}. Hours planned: {col:load.hours} against {col:load.capacity_hours} hours of capacity.
Load percent: {col:load.load_pct}. Free hours: {col:load.free_hours}. Load flag: {col:load.flag}.
If the load is over capacity, ask the head baker to move a cake to another day before the day starts.
Bake list for the oven of {set:company} on {col:oven.date}, dated {today}.
Tray loads booked: {col:oven.tray_loads} of {col:oven.block_capacity}. Free trays: {col:oven.free_trays}. Block load: {col:oven.block_load}. Flag: {col:oven.flag}.
A tray load is one full tray in the oven. Fix a block marked over capacity before the bake starts.
Order calendar entry for a due date
Order calendar of {set:company}, dated {today}. Order {col:orders.order_id} for {col:orders.client}.
Due on {col:orders.due_date} ({col:orders.due_day}), {col:orders.fulfil}, time window {col:orders.window}. Days to the due date: {col:orders.days_to_due}. Start the work on {col:orders.prep_start}.
Order placed on {col:orders.order_date}, lead time {col:orders.lead_days} days, check: {col:orders.rush}. Status: {col:orders.status}.
Period: {col:peaks.period}, from {col:peaks.from_date} to {col:peaks.to_date} ({col:peaks.length} days). It starts in {col:peaks.days_to_start} days. State: {col:peaks.state}.
Expected orders: {col:peaks.expected_orders}, about {col:peaks.orders_day} a day. Extra staff hours: {col:peaks.extra_hours}, about {col:peaks.hours_day} a day.
Book the helpers, order the stock and check the daily cake limits before the first day of the peak.
Last service: {col:equip.last_service}. Next service: {col:equip.next_service}, which is {col:equip.days_to_service} days from today. Service flag: {col:equip.flag}.
Write what the technician did and keep this report with the equipment. Check your own local rules on equipment checks.
Team schedule line for a shift
{col:shifts.person} ({col:shifts.role}) works on {col:shifts.date}, starting at {col:shifts.start_time}, for {col:shifts.shift_hours} hours.
Print one line for each shift of the week and give the sheet to the team on the first day.
Standing order bake sheet of {set:company}, dated {today}.
Account: {col:so.account}. Product: {col:so.product}. Units a week: {col:so.units_week}, delivered on {col:so.weekdays} ({col:so.delivery_days} days).
Bake {col:so.units_delivery} units for each delivery, which is {col:so.trays_delivery} tray loads. Status: {col:so.status}.
Renewal date: {col:so.renewal_date}, {col:so.days_to_renewal} days from today. Renewal flag: {col:so.renew_flag}.
Production capacity summary for a day
Production capacity summary of {set:company} for {col:plan.date}, dated {today}.
Oven load {col:plan.oven_load} ({col:plan.oven_flag}), fridge load {col:plan.fridge_load} ({col:plan.fridge_flag}), staff load {col:plan.staff_load}.
Capacity rules: {set:oven_trays} tray loads in a normal day, {set:fridge_slots} fridge slots overnight, a person is overloaded above {set:overload_pct} of their day.

Open Start and type your company name and your own rules in the yellow cells: oven tray loads, fridge slots, overload share, shift hours, rush rule and the days to start a cake.
Type every order to bake on Orders due. The days to the due date, the day to start the work and the rush check fill in. Copy the first row to see a full order.
Write each bake, fill and cover, decorate and pack task on Production tasks with the day, the person and the hours. Mark the status when the task is done, and the flag shows what is overdue.
Read Workload by person every morning: hours against the hours a person can work, the load percent and the overload flag. Move work before the day starts, not during it.
Daily plan shows the orders, the hours and the oven and fridge load of each day. Days marked nearly full or over capacity need a decision: move work, add a helper or close the day to new orders.
Fill Standing orders with the weekly products of cafes and shops. The units for each delivery and the tray loads show what to bake on each delivery day.
Use Bake batches and Oven schedule to plan the oven by time block, and Fridge plan to hold finished items overnight.
Keep the Decorating queue current: the hours each cake needs, the days left and the hours needed each day show which cake is running out of time.
Check Ingredient needs by day for shortages and keep the Prep list for the work done before a bake. Use Shifts and Time off to plan who works.
Write every Delay and every Rework: minutes or hours lost, the reason and the cost. Read them each month to see what to fix.
Plan Holiday peaks early and keep Equipment service dates. Capacity rules holds the limits you check the plan against.

Use the 14 calculators before you decide: day load, oven and fridge, bake date, batch size, recipe quantity, decorator time, staff hours, overtime, standing order, rush fit, peak week, delay cost and a what-if grid.
Print 10 sheets and 10 documents, follow 10 checklists and tap a message link to open a chat with the text already written (28 messages). Read the Dashboard and Charts every week.
Know what is on the shelf, what to buy and what you throw away
Stock, purchasing, supplier prices and waste for home bakeries and cake studios
Stock against reorder point by item
every ingredient and packaging item shows what is on hand, its reorder point, a status and the quantity to order, with out of stock items marked
what the week needs against the shelf gives the quantity to buy, the packs and the cost for each supplier
the daily use turns the shelf into days of cover, so you see which item runs out before the next delivery
each lot shows the days left, the value at risk and a flag, and the calculator says which lot to use first
waste of ingredients and finished products with its cost and reason, and the waste share of the ingredient spend against your target
each quote shows the saving against the current price, whether it is cheaper or dearer and whether it is still valid
Price rise impact on stock value
every price change shows the change in percent, and the calculator shows how a rise changes the value of the stock on the shelf
each delivery is checked in with the reference and the issues, and every supplier problem keeps its credit and days open
counted against the system with the difference, its value and a result, so a gap is found while it is small
a budget for each week against what was spent, with what is left and an over budget flag

One row for each ingredient and packaging item with what is on hand, the reorder point and the daily use; the status, days of cover, quantity to order and stock value fill in.
Purchases with the amount and the month
One row for each purchase with the quantity, the unit cost and who it was bought from; the amount and the month fill in, so spending by month, category and supplier is always up to date.
Purchase orders with the expected date and days late
One row for each order placed with a supplier with the expected date and the date it arrived; the total, the days late and an on time flag fill in, so a late delivery stands out.
Suppliers with lead time and payment terms
The six suppliers with the days they need to deliver and the days you have to pay; reorder points and the purchase orders use the lead days.
Ingredients with unit cost, allergens and shelf days
The 38 ingredients and packaging items with the cost for each kilogram or piece, the allergens and how long they keep; stock, purchases and recipes read the cost from here.
Ingredient usage by month from the recipes
The kilograms or pieces of each main ingredient used every month, taken from what was baked; the cost and the months of cover fill in, so you see which ingredients drive spending.
Recipe lines with the cost of each line
One row for each ingredient of each recipe in grams or pieces; the cost of the line comes from the ingredient price, so a price rise shows in the recipe at once.
Products with servings, ingredient cost and shelf days
The 24 products with servings, the ingredient cost of one unit and how long it keeps; the cost per serving fills in.
Ingredient price changes with the change in percent
One row for each time a supplier changed the price of an ingredient, with the old and the new cost; the change in percent fills in, so a price rise is seen the month it happens.
One row for each time something was thrown away: an ingredient or a finished product, how much, what it cost and why; the team reads the reasons to stop the same loss.
Waste against ingredient spend by month
One row for each month with the waste of ingredients, the waste of finished products, the ingredient spend and the revenue; the waste share and the spend share of revenue fill in.
Stock counts with the difference and its value
One row for each item counted on the shelf with the quantity counted and the quantity the system expects; the difference, its value and a result fill in, so a gap is found while it is small.
Expiry watch with days left and value at risk
One row for each lot of a perishable item with its best-before date and quantity; the days left, the value at risk and a use-first flag fill in, so nothing expires unseen.
Shopping list with what to buy and the cost
One row for each item the coming week needs against what is on the shelf; the quantity to buy, the packs and the cost fill in, so the list for each supplier is ready before you order.
Goods received with an issue flag
One row for each delivery checked in with the supplier, the reference on the delivery note, the lines checked and the issues found; the issue flag fills in.
Supplier issues with the credit received
One row for each problem with a supplier: short, damaged, wrong or late items, a price that differs; the credit and the status are kept and the days open fill in.
Supplier quotes against the current price
One row for each quote with the offered price for each kilogram or piece and the day it is valid until; the current price, the saving and a cheaper or dearer flag fill in.
Low stock log with the days to restock
One row each time an item fell to or below its reorder point, with what was done; the days to restock and a restocked flag fill in, so slow reorders show up.
Weekly purchase budget with what is left
One row for each week with the budget for ingredients and packaging and what was spent; what is left, the share used and a flag fill in, so spending stays in check.
